stem: A bank offers a nominal interest rate of 12% per annum, compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate of interest? [Use: (1.01) raised to the power 12 = 1.1268]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Effective rate = (1 + 0.12/12) raised to the power 12 - 1 = (1.01) raised to the power 12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 0.1268 = 12.68%.
Student treats the nominal rate as the effective rate, ignoring compounding within the year.
Student uses (1 + 0.12/2)² - 1, treating monthly compounding as semi-annual: (1.06)² - 1 = 0.1236.
Student computes 1.1268 - 1.01 = 0.1168, subtracting one monthly factor instead of 1.

explanation: Effective annual rate = (1 + r/m)^m - 1, where r = 0.12 and m = 12. This gives (1.01)^12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 0.1268 = 12.68%. The nominal rate 12% ignores within-year compounding, so it understates the true return.

explanation_sections.punchline: The formula for effective annual rate is (1 + r/m)^m minus 1. With r = 0.12 and m = 12, the periodic rate is 0.01, and the stem gives (1.01)^12 = 1.1268, so the effective rate is 12.68%.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula and map the givens: effective rate = (1 + r/m)^m minus 1. Here r = 0.12, m = 12, giving r/m = 0.01. The stem provides (1.01)^12 = 1.1268 to avoid manual computation. Subtract 1 to get 0.1268, then convert to percentage: 12.68%. The only formula choice is whether to use the nominal rate as-is (wrong) or raise the periodic factor to the power m.
explanation_sections.lesson: The effective rate always exceeds the nominal rate when m is greater than 1. Returning the nominal rate 12% unchanged is the most common error; it ignores that compounding within the year earns interest on interest.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. The stem gives the power value directly. Subtract 1, convert to percent: 10 seconds of work. Reject option (2) in three seconds: 12% is the nominal rate restated, not the effective rate. Reject option (1) in three seconds: 12.36% would require semi-annual compounding, not monthly.
